The accessible name contains the SVG's aria-label ('Your Privacy Choices Opt-Out Icon') concatenated with the visible link text ('Your Privacy Choices'), producing 'Your Privacy Choices Opt-Out Icon Your Privacy Choices'. Visible text 'Your Privacy Choices' IS contained in the accessible name (2.5.3 passes). However the accessible name is unnecessarily verbose — 'Opt-Out Icon' is implementation detail that pollutes the link announcement. The duplicate repetition of 'Your Privacy Choices' at the end is a 4.1.2 quality issue. The SVG should be aria-hidden (it is decorative within the link); instead its aria-label='Your Privacy Choices Opt-Out Icon' is exposed, creating a verbose and confusing name. Flagged as a 4.1.2 concern (name quality).

name-role-state.evidence: SVG has role='img' and aria-label='Your Privacy Choices Opt-Out Icon'. The SVG is inside the <a> link for 'Your Privacy Choices'. As a decorative icon within a labeled link, the SVG should be aria-hidden (not role='img' with its own name), because its name is already communicated by the link's text. The current setup causes the SVG name to be concatenated into the link's accessible name (creating the verbose 'Opt-Out Icon Your Privacy Choices' compound). The SVG is not independently meaningful — it is a decorative regulatory opt-out icon that should carry aria-hidden='true'. Flagging as 1.1.1 (image exposed when it should be hidden as decorative-within-link).
